title: Genome builds and lift-over

blocks.what_we_do: We convert the separate GRCh37 exercise to GRCh38 in R. We use a chain file for this one direction. We keep the exercise apart from the main analysis.
blocks.why:
GRCh37 and GRCh38 are two different reference assemblies of the human genome. A coordinate is a chromosome and a position in one named assembly. Changing the build label or the rsID does not change the coordinates.

A [lift-over](docs/glossary.md#lift-over) converts coordinates from one assembly to the other. It uses a [chain file](docs/glossary.md#chain-file), which records which intervals of the two genomes are aligned. After a lift-over, a site can be unmapped (it has no match), it can move to another chromosome, or it can map to the reverse strand.

UCSC intervals are zero-based and half-open, which means they start counting at 0 and exclude the end point. The course positions are one-based, which means they start counting at 1. Review the unmapped sites and the reverse-strand sites. Do not accept a conversion that nobody documented.
blocks.you_need: You need the small GRCh37 exercise supplied at 0.5. You also need the official hg19-to-hg38 chain file. It is part of the course data, in the folder `data/course/grch37_exercise/`. You do not need to download it. The main array is already GRCh38, so we do not lift it again.
blocks.command:
```{r s2-6}
legacy <- file.path(cfg$data_dir, "grch37_exercise", "legacy_grch37")
bim37 <- read_ws(paste0(legacy, ".bim"), header = FALSE)
chain <- file.path(cfg$data_dir, "grch37_exercise", "hg19ToHg38.over.chain.gz")
require_files(chain)
lifted <- guided_liftover(paste0("chr", bim37[[1]]), bim37[[4]], chain)
keep <- !is.na(lifted$position) & lifted$chromosome == paste0("chr", bim37[[1]])
map <- data.frame(ID = bim37[[2]][keep], POS = lifted$position[keep])
map_file <- guided_path(cfg, "2.6", "update_map.tsv")
write.table(map, map_file, sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE)
keep_file <- guided_list(map$ID, guided_path(cfg, "2.6", "mapped.txt"))
args <- c("--bfile", legacy, "--extract", keep_file, "--update-map", map_file)
reverse <- bim37[[2]][keep & lifted$strand == "-"]
if (length(reverse)) args <- c(args, "--flip", guided_list(reverse, guided_path(cfg, "2.6", "reverse.txt")))
run_plink(cfg, c(args, "--make-pgen", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "2.6", "grch38")))
ann <- guided_table(file.path(cfg$data_dir, "array", "sim2026_array_annotation.tsv"))
k <- match(map$ID, ann$Name)
stopifnot(all(map$POS[!is.na(k)] == as.numeric(ann$Position_GRCh38[k[!is.na(k)]])))
print(c(input_sites = nrow(bim37), mapped_same_chromosome = sum(keep), reverse_strand = length(reverse)))
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
bin/plink2 --bfile data/course/grch37_exercise/legacy_grch37 --extract results/guided/s2-6_mapped.txt --update-map results/guided/s2-6_update_map.tsv --make-pgen --out results/guided/s2-6_grch38 --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

`--extract` keeps only the IDs that were mapped successfully; `--update-map` reads the ID and the new position from two columns. If R finds reverse-strand mappings, add `--flip` with the reverse list that R generates. The exercise keeps only the sites that stay on the same chromosome, and it reports the sites it excludes. `--out` sets the prefix of the output file names. `--threads 2` limits PLINK to two worker threads. `--memory 2048` sets the memory budget to 2048 MiB. The R helper prints the exact command with your own safe paths.
blocks.expected_result:
The exercise has 10,000 sites. 9,970 of them map to the same chromosome, and eight of these map to the reverse strand in this chain file. PLINK prints a warning that the base-pair positions are now unsorted. This warning is expected: the new GRCh38 positions are not in the old order. The resulting exercise variants are not sorted by position. Sort them explicitly before any operation that needs sorted input. Mapped positions whose identifier also appears in the course annotation agree with GRCh38. The main 296,510-site state from 2.5 is unchanged. A lift-over can lose sites, so record the mapping counts that are reported.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks and the expected counts passed on Windows.
blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error message. Check the input file named in the message. Check that the previous step finished. Keep the command and the console output (the text printed in R). Do not use files from a different version of the dataset. See [troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.what_this_check_can_reveal: It can reveal build mismatches, gaps and reverse mappings. A chain file does not check alleles and does not impute genotypes.
blocks.quick_check:
Does a successful position lift-over guarantee that REF and ALT now match the destination reference?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. You must still check the alleles and the reverse-strand mappings.

</details>
blocks.files_created: `s2-6_update_map.tsv`, the mapped and reverse lists, and the separate `s2-6_grch38` files.
